Simply put, one of the best modern stealth games done from a first person perspective ever; in gameplay, story, and most of all, the world building atmosphere. No other game or piece of fiction is quite like dishonored in it's fantastic blend of a victorian england esque world with whale oil powered technology, a rat plague ravaging the city, and a mysterious old god known only as "the outsider" along with all the related mysterious occult and magic.
The only cons for this game I can think of are that it actively punishes you for doing things lethally vs nonlethally unlike in say deus ex where it was just slightly reduced experience points or whatever (dead bodies attract rats and killing too much leads to the bad ending), and the fact that you cannot go back and redo missions to get any runes, bone charms, or w/e collectibles you've missed the first time around (you CAN replay but what you collect does not carry over to your current progress) means that if you are a completionist/power gamer, you'll need to get it all on the first go, so save often and look things up/use a guide if necessary.
Otherwise, only other thing is that the facial models and animation look rather garish but I mean come on, everything else looks fantastic for a game from 2012.
If you're thinking of getting into dishonored with dishonored 2, please hold your horses and give this a play first. I guarantee this game will not disappoint, and the same goes for the "knife of dunwall" and "brigmore witches" DLCs.

I decided to make this game my first yuri visual novel, and I am glad to say that it has not left me disappointed. This game is about 20 hours long if you don't use a guide and if you skip shared content between the routes.
Likely the largest make-or-break points for a visual novel is its localisation. JAST has reasonably good track record, as they also had Steins;Gate localised, and that game's localisation turned out very well. They have done a reasonably good job on this one, with very few points where I would disagree with how they've translated it, and very infrequent typos and formatting errors. If I could say something, it was how the additional content unlocked upon completely clearing the game was handled. The comic was localised in Comic Sans (with typos and poor wording aplenty) and the VA comments are not subbed (kinda annoying because I was interested in what they had to say). They also have this weird pechant for having inconsistent writing of names. 'Rikka' is written a couple times sas 'Rika' and 'Dalia' is written as 'Daliah' in the portrait (so on the same screen). Not big things, sorta annoying but you get over it fast.
Next is the art (of course), which is very nice. Watercolour-esque character portraits, with a range of expressions. These are nice, but the contrast is a bit low so they appear very bright in night scenes. There are an average number of CGs scattered across the game, sharing the nice watercolour style. Again, a small complaint is that the backgrounds, while still beautifully done, don't really fit the style of the (IMO) beautiful portraits.
There are multiple routes in this game
and this is controlled by a reasonably unique system. If I could sort of explain it, it would be somewhat like Mass Effect, with different 'tones' of responses
You can tell which one you've picked by the little jingle that plays after you make a plot selection which causes a change in the flower in the bottom right corner, which changes the plot depending on its status. This has good and bad points. The good points is that you know which way you're leading the path, but the bad point is that
and so you're obliged to keep restarting from the last choice to pick the one you want
With these points in mind, the story is sorta linear and you don't get anything / you can't jump between routes.
Well time for a spoiler block as I speak about the plot, no real plot spoilers but gameplay and theme spoilers
I found the story very balanced and varied throughout the 20-ish hours I played the game.
Throughout the game, there is a mystery solving process that happens in multiple chapters, increasing in complexity as the story progresses. These are done in a 'thinking' section where you are usually asked 3 questions, each with 3-4 options. The idea is that you can think back to the events of that chapter in question and spot the important clues for the case you are solving. You are obliged to select all the  correct answers and solve the case to continue
Some people claim that with careful reading and detective work, these are logical. I disagree wholeheartedly. I feel that these are dodgy reverse Cluedo, where you only get the clues and information that you'd have needed to solve the case AFTER you make the correct selections in the 'thinking' section that requires them! There's lots of points where there is the most obscure trivia that you'd have needed to know, and one point, where they ask you for a real life statistic which if you use the exact wording they ask for, will not accept the RL answer
. In the end these sections turn into a brute force attempt as you keep reloading and inputting sequential results to beat the completely stacked odds against you to concoct some stupid conspiracy like story of events that happened. Fortunately, there's only 4-5 of these in the game. I like the mystery element, but these sections are annoying.
Overall, this is a pretty damn good game. It's definitely worth your money at sale price. Conclusion, plot's good, art's good, gameplay's unique but that mystery element is linking random plots together in a conspiracy theory levels of logic.

This game dont want to be the next DayZ. this game dont pretend to be a "HUGE SANDBOX SURVIVAL ZOMBIE EXPLORATION" ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t, it is what it is... and that is where it shines. I had very low expectations about this one, but after entering the game i was sucked-in by its rich atmosphere, the day and night cicles, the ♥♥♥♥ing weather cicle. At night you'll get ambushed, during storms you'll get confused by not being able to hear that good, the atmosphere will change when you get greedy and get the attention of a horde.
On top of all that, you can craft a place to call home, you'll spend your time looting every place you come across, repeating missions over and over just to improve your character and not die that often. You'll be surprised by all the possibilities this game offers and by the looks of it the developers are giving this game a LOT of attention and care.

Best Tom Clancy game in a while though, would recommend to anyone who is a fan of the franchise.

Open world, but all scripted, not dynamic. Once you've seen a small amount of the content, you've seen all of the content. The world reacts in independent, deterministic, compartmentalized ways to your actions. The shooting and stealth mechanics are disappointing and offer a shallow experience.

The single player team AI sucks and when you use sync shot with AI, it's unrealistic in a lot of situations and made me feel like I was cheating. Enemy AI would sometimes spawn real close while doing rebel upgrade missions and I could see them suddenly spawning in out of nowhere which took the immersion out. Every now and then I would get stuck in an outcropping of rocks, like a trap you can fall into but can't climb out of. Plane physics seemed unrealistic.. even though I wasn't looking for a realistic simulation, it still bugged me.  I felt like I was playing a Far Cry game with a Tom Clancy theme.  The character customization also needs more options. There are in game purchases, but it doesn't even seem to help much with the variety.
I had several other gripes, but for some reason I still really enjoy this game and play it often.
Even though wind doesn't come into affect with the bullet physics while sniping, it is still enjoyable. Co-op is fun. There's a nice realism to the variation of vehicles in the game. There's a good variety of guns and optics/attachments with changable mags and stocks too for most guns. The graphics and weather effects are real good too. You can also toggle a lot of the HUD elements to your liking.
I'd recommend not playing it on the easier difficulties though, unless you're into that sort of thing.

It can't be disabled.  Some like it, but many have complained about it.  Why they felt the need to do this differently to the original TDU and every other racing game, you'd have to ask them. I probably should not have started off with the negative, but it's best to be honest up front. It should go without saying, but this game has a ways to go before it's truly great. There are various glitches/bugs, and there are weapons, and tools, but I could see so many more versions and improvements of those being added in the future. The wild life is ruthless, which can be a little annoying at times, and they can be a little difficult to hit with a pistol with some mouse lag. That last part could be my mouse acceleration, but who knows. With that said the development team has left a massive amount of 'space' for this title to grow towards its true potential. What does that mean? That's where the positive portion of my review comes in..
Let's talk graphics. On my 980ti, I'm getting around 25 fps in 4k. For me, that's not bad at all. All I did was blow in the cartridge, slam that sucker in, reach up to the knob on the TV and crank the graphics to max. Even with that, the game performs nicely. The wildlife looks great, and the effects and lighting are great as well.
The sounds and ambiance are superb. Meteors and the worm will startle you if you're not expecting them.
The combat is a little touchy in that if you have mouse acceleration turned on, the effect of that may cause your cross-hair to move slower than your hand/eye. Again, this could just be my own error. I'm not particularly good at shooters either so I'm a little slow on the draw.
Stat driven-ish.. So you have to level up various categories of actions that will give you advancement points of sorts to move along the "technology tree". Leveling up these tasks does not currently make you perform those tasks any better. However, there is a mechanic as you level your character up you're able to attribute points into carry weight, run speed. health, and stamina(is it?). These are simple and meaningful.
Other pros that I have found thus far:
-   Base Building is robust enough to keep you busy for a while, but lacking in that you'll want more once you finish building.
-   Day and night cycles offer a sense of time while playing the game. They also have their own challenges. I've notices that during the day/light cycle more players are out and about. At night, more of the alien wildlife patrols. The night is really dark too. You have to use a flashlight in most cases.
-   Vehicular combat looks promising. There are small agile vehicles that can be crafted. They're great for farming wildlife, and the more bulky vehicles are great for farming everything else.
-   MY FAVORITE! Mechs. So far I have found a quick and nimble mech spider mount thing that is great for scouting. Then, there's the mech in the picture above. It's been a while since I've gotten to play a game with mechs in it and actually enjoyed the combat. It's clunky and imperfect, but it feels good. Kind of sad that a game not designed as a mech game did it better than most of the actual mech games. I blame Bandai.
**All in all, my friends and myself are having some real fun on this game, and I hope that others will come to support this title as well.
